messages:
inc-bot: [ALERT] Network egress error rate spike detected in eu-west-1 -> upstream ProviderZ (packet loss + BGP withdraws). Paging net-oncall immediately :rotating_light:
net-oncall (Miguel): Got the page, I'm on it. Seeing 8–15% packet loss on a subset of carrier links, many prefixes intermittently withdraw.
sre-ash: I can join — hitting our vanity endpoints from eu-west-1 shows failures for about 30% of requests, TL;DR customer impact on search/embeddings ingestion.
net-oncall (Miguel): Initial checks: BGP sessions to ProviderZ show flaps on 3 peers, AS path changes for transit routes, and some prefixes blackholing. Provider portal showing partial outage in their AMS PoP.
eng-infra-lead (Leah): Can we route around at the edge? Any fallback provider with capacity?
peering-team: We have standing backups with TransitY and TransitQ; we can shift announced prefixes to TransitQ but need a short plan to avoid route churn.
net-oncall (Miguel): Plan: 1) Announce de-preferences to ProviderZ for non-critical prefixes (localpref -50) 2) Gradually prep withdraw/announce on TransitQ for critical subnets 3) Enable HC redirect at LBs for eu-west-1 -> eu-central for ingestion endpoints. Will execute in canary.
dns-oncall (Priya): Noted customer DNS observations: increased NXDOMAIN retries and SERVFAILs for some resolver paths, likely due to upstream packet loss to authoritative edges. Suggest increasing TTL tolerance for affected records while we stabilize.
sre-ash: Quick mitigation request: flip the L7 healthcheck timeout in eu-west-1 to 10s and failover threshold to 2 to reduce noisy retries, then route traffic to eu-central for critical writes.
net-oncall (Miguel): Executing canary: adjusting BGP localpref for 52.192.0.0/14 and 34.240.0.0/16 to prefer TransitQ. Applying on two edge routers now.
network-ops: (reaction: :thumbsup:) Noted — we'll watch BGP convergence. Expected RIB churn ~30s per router.
eng-infra-lead (Leah): Initiating LB redirect playbook: updating haproxy map for ingestion.* to point to eu-central pool, applying gradually to a small % first.
peering-team: ProviderZ responded via ticket: "We're investigating a flap in AMS due to upstream fabric instability; working on hardware-level fix." They've marked high severity.
net-oncall (Miguel): After canary: traffic for the two prefixes is now converging to TransitQ; packet loss on affected flows dropped from 12% -> 1.2%. BGP sessions stabilized for those prefixes.
dns-oncall (Priya): DNS SERVFAILs reduced after reroute; still seeing some TTL edge-caching misbehavior. I'll trigger emergency revalidation for glue records and bump retention windows.
sre-ash: Customer impact assessment: ~4% of active requests in EU saw elevated errors between 08:02–08:20 UTC; ingestion backlog increased by ~18% for that window. No data corruption, mostly retries/timeouts.
cust-succ (Jordan): I'm drafting a notice for customers who hit ingest SLA that could be affected. Will wait for final numbers but flagging customers on Dedicated and Private.
net-oncall (Miguel): Follow-ups: 1) Keep ProviderZ ticket on follow 2) Leave TransitQ pref for 30m then slowly rebalance 3) Postmortem lead?
sre-ash: I'll take postmortem. Please capture BGP RIB snaps, netflow from edge, and LB metrics.
eng-infra-lead (Leah): Metrics to capture: request error rate per-region, queue/backlog sizes, LB failover counts, and healthcheck timeouts.
peering-team: We'll coordinate with ProviderZ for root cause timeline and request BGP debug logs.
net-oncall (Miguel): Standing down page for now — symptoms reduced and critical routes stable. Keeping channel open for followups and RCA.
inc-bot: [INCIDENT STATUS] mitigated -> monitoring. Escalation level: P2.
sre-ash: Postmortem kickoff scheduled in 2 hours. tagging @peering-team @dns-oncall for timelines.
cust-succ (Jordan): I'll update customers with the mitigation summary once you confirm the final window and affected prefixes.
network-ops: Logged all command diffs and config commits to infra-audit.
net-oncall (Miguel): Final note: If ProviderZ doesn't provide root cause by EOD, we'll request a more permanent pref shift and consider capacity bump on TransitQ for eu-west-1.
sre-ash: Thanks everyone — excellent cross-team runbook execution.
